criteria.name: goal_alignment
criteria.description: The planned final outcome directly achieves the original objective with relevant, minimal sufficient scope.

anchors.1: Outcome is explicit, achievable and fully aligned with the requested scope.
anchors.0.25: Some relevant work, but the central outcome is not achievable as written.
anchors.0.5: Outcome is addressed only in part or includes material scope drift.
anchors.0.75: Outcome is achievable with only minor scope clarification needed.

criteria.name: task_fulfillment
criteria.description: The plan covers each explicit functional requirement and respects each stated constraint; identify concrete omissions here.

anchors.0: No requested functionality or constraints are addressed.
anchors.1: Every explicit requirement and constraint maps to a concrete planned action.
anchors.0.25: A critical requirement or constraint is absent or violated.
anchors.0.5: Several requirements are addressed but a material requirement remains incomplete.
anchors.0.75: All essential requirements and constraints are covered, with minor details open.

criteria.name: request_understanding
criteria.description: The plan interprets the original problem, terminology and assumptions correctly without substituting another task.

anchors.1: Interpretation is precise and all necessary assumptions are stated and supported.
anchors.0.25: A central concept or assumption is substantially misunderstood.
anchors.0.5: Interpretation is partly right but contains a material ambiguity or unsupported assumption.
anchors.0.75: Interpretation is correct with minor assumptions needing clarification.

criteria.name: code_correctness
criteria.description: The proposed technical approach is feasible given supplied APIs/context, with logically consistent dependencies and edge-case handling. Do not assert that code ran.

anchors.0: The supplied evidence contradicts the central technical approach.
anchors.1: Approach, dependencies and necessary edge-case handling are fully supported and coherent.
anchors.0.25: A blocking technical error or impossible dependency would prevent success.
anchors.0.5: Approach is plausible but a material technical gap threatens execution.
anchors.0.75: Approach is feasible and coherent with only minor technical details open.

criteria.name: code_completeness
criteria.description: The plan provides actionable, ordered implementation steps, necessary verification and a clear completion condition. Judge execution detail here, not requirement coverage again.

anchors.0: No actionable implementation or verification route exists.
anchors.1: All necessary steps, dependencies, verification expectations and completion conditions are explicit.
anchors.0.25: Steps are too vague or disordered to execute the main work.
anchors.0.5: Work can start but material ordering, verification or completion details are missing.
anchors.0.75: Work and necessary verification are actionable, with minor detail left open.

weight_origin: Existing Exaix CRITERIA weights; no empirical optimization or universal SOTA claim.
required_tag_semantics: legacy metadata; no additional veto; all result keys must be present

insufficient_evidence.missingEvidence: nonempty array of input names; exclusive union arm; no numeric score or label

provider_policy.model_identifiers: explicit validated identifiers required at activation
provider_policy.settings: record supported applied settings and CLI defaults; do not infer unsupported temperature or seed

activation: Pending typed schema, explicit --judge-profile wiring, shared frozen input, complete result validation and Phase 146 security/identity tests
